alternatives.description: Let current loaders fail first and require users to invoke a separate manual upgrade.
disadvantages: Makes ordinary operations fail before they can report or repair compatibility.
Leaves upgrade behavior inconsistent across entry points.
rejectedBecause: Readiness must run before strict current loaders at every public operation entry.

advantages: Makes version inspection simple after startup.
alternatives.description: Write the current package version before migrating project data.
disadvantages: A crash can hide incomplete publication behind version equality.
Recovery cannot distinguish prepared from fully published state.
rejectedBecause: Configuration is updated last and a durable pending marker survives interruption.

alternatives.description: Treat the new version check or access heartbeat as sufficient to fence old processes.
disadvantages: Already-running old code need not read or honor the new marker.
It cannot establish writer quiescence for the first legacy upgrade.
rejectedBecause: The previous installed runner must be held across an upgrade test and receive a supported restart, refusal, or recovery disposition that prevents corruption.

advantages: Reuses the future migration machinery for the initial conversion.
alternatives.description: Ship a sealed migration and legacy compatibility reader for Projector's own JSON-to-TOML conversion.
disadvantages: Permanently carries a one-time internal transition and dual-format premise.
rejectedBecause: The user explicitly waived a formal migrator for the one-time conversion; the permanent framework starts from the verified converted baseline.

assumptions: All compatible installed runners honor the shared operation-access protocol after the converted baseline.
The host can resolve a writable user Codex data directory for verified backups.
The existing writer lease and transaction journal remain the canonical mutation exclusion and recovery mechanisms inside ordinary governed writes.
The one-time legacy conversion can require a supported process or session restart because older code cannot be retroactively fenced.
payload.rationale: The user requires installed Projector operations to prepare compatible project data automatically before strict loaders run, with numeric SemVer chains, checksummed immutable migrations, exclusive migration access, a verified full backup under the user's Codex data directory, recoverable staging and publication, and configuration updated last. Existing transaction journals and receipts are durable recovery evidence, not disposable caches. A new version marker cannot stop an older already-running process that does not participate in the new protocol; the legacy transition therefore requires an explicit supported restart/quiescence disposition and a held-old-process negative test before promotion.
